$\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1 \Rightarrow k\int_0^1 (x^3 - x^5)\,dx = 1$

Since $\displaystyle\int_0^1 (x^3 - x^5)\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^4}{4} - \dfrac{x^6}{6}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

then $\dfrac{k}{12} = 1 \Rightarrow k = 12$

Let $x = M$ be the median of model $g$. Then:

$\dfrac{1}{2} = \displaystyle\int_0^M g(x)\,dx = \int_0^M 2x\,dx = \left[x^2\right]_0^M = M^2$, i.e. $M^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Consider $\displaystyle\int_0^M f(x)\,dx = \int_0^M 12(x^3 - x^5)\,dx = \left[3x^4 - 2x^6\right]_0^M = 3M^4 - 2M^6$

Since $M^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $\displaystyle\int_0^M f(x)\,dx = 3\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence $x = M$ is also the median of model $f$, i.e. the two models have the same median.
